chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Awf al-Bajali, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The ablution before the meal and after it both increase in the livelihood.' And it is reported that Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Its first (ablution before the meal) negates poverty, and its end (ablution after the meal) negates worries.'
ai.seo_question: What are the benefits of performing ablution before and after eating according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kulayni’s *Al-Kafi*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) underscores the ritual purification (wudu) as a means of spiritual and material blessing, linking physical cleanliness to divine provision. The tradition further distinguishes the specific benefits: pre-meal wudu alleviates poverty, while post-meal wudu dispels anxiety, reflecting the Shia emphasis on integrating daily acts of worship with holistic well-being.
